newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Election revote held on Indonesia's Madura island.
newsitem.headline: Election revote held on Indonesia's Madura island.

text.p: Indonesia held an unprecedented revote on Madura island on Wednesday after angry Moslems alleging vote rigging burned ballot boxes there following last week's general elections.
Some of more than 40,000 registered voters trickled to the 86 voting stations after the six-hour polling period opened at 8 a.m. (0100 GMT) in Madura's Sampang district.
The official Antara news agency quoted East Java military commander Major-General Imam Utomo as saying he had issued a "shoot on the spot" order to guarantee security for the revote.

"There will be no compromise against anybody who tries to riot and foil the revote. I have issued a warning to shoot on the spot rioters and those who try to foil the revote," Antara quoted him as saying.
East Java police chief Major-General Sumarsono said in Sampang on Wednesday there had been no problems as voting started. "It's all calm. You can see for yourself," he told Reuters.

The island off the East Java coast is a stronghold of the Moslem-backed United Development Party (PPP), and a mob went on the rampage after last Thursday's general elections and burned the Sampang ballot boxes on reports that the ruling Golkar party had swept the polls.
Golkar won more than 74 percent of the vote nation-wide for the 425 elected seats in the House of Representatives in the polls held every five years, up from 68 percent in the previous vote in 1992.

The PPP won almost 23 percent, up from 17 percent. The only other legal party, the fragmented Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI) nose dived to three percent from 15 percent. Locals residents said it was unclear how many people would take part in the Madura revote after the local PPP branch said it would close its doors on Wednesday and not provide witnesses for the polling booths.
"Who knows if they will all come? What is important is that they have all received a written invitation to come," one polling booth official in Sampang town said.
Hasan Asy'ari, local secretary of the PPP's Sampang branch, said the party was not advocating an actual boycott of the poll, which is illegal in Indonesia.

"If the PPP does not join the revote, it will be to their own detriment. If they do not want to participate, this is within the regulations," East Java Governor Basofi Soedirman was quoted as saying in the Surabaya-based Surya paper on Wednesday.
In Jakarta, PPP leaders have charged there were widespread irregularities in last week's vote. The party is due to meet on Thursday to decide whether to accept the election result.
Indonesia witnessed its most violent election campaign in three decades in the run-up to the poll, with much of the trouble between supporters of the PPP and Golkar.
Economic analysts are keeping a wary eye on the PPP decision in case a refusal to accept the vote prompts further violence.

"If the rules are violated, then the people are unhappy. If they are obeyed, then they are happy," influential local Moslem leader Alawy Muhammad, who was also a PPP national campaigner, said in an interview at Sampang.

PPP branch secretary Asy'ari said on Tuesday the PPP had recorded violations at all 1,033 polling stations in the Sampang regency and wanted the revote at all these places rather than just the 86 stations in the central Sampang district.

The revote is centred on a sleepy seaside town of about 100,000 people. People travelling into Sampang on Wednesday from outer districts had their vehicles stopped and searched by armed police and soldiers. Young men were body searched for knives and other weapons.
